title.en: Filament length conservation in a shortening sarcomere

summary: Confirm that filament lengths stay fixed while overlap changes within the valid shortening range, using the declared reject or clamp policy for invalid requests.
objective: Filament lengths remain constant and A-band width is preserved as Z separation changes within the valid range; the declared reject or clamp policy prevents invalid committed geometry.
applies_when: A scene illustrates contraction by sliding overlapping elements.
Band or zone labels are derived from element boundaries.
A viewer can drive a shortening parameter to its extremes.
intent_signals: the whole sarcomere shrinks when it contracts
check the band widths during shortening
example_prompts: Check that the filaments keep their length while this sarcomere shortens.

principles: In the sliding-filament picture the filaments do not change length; what changes is their overlap, so filament length is a model constant and band widths are derived from it.
The A band is set by thick-filament length and therefore holds while Z discs approach; a model that scales the whole sarcomere uniformly contradicts the mechanism it illustrates.
Specify the valid shortening range and apply its declared reject or clamp policy before committing geometry. An out-of-range request must not silently create an invalid configuration.
implementation: Parametrize by Z-disc separation with thick and thin filament lengths as fixed constants, and derive the A band, I band and any central zone from those constants.
Evaluate at five shortening values including both ends of the authored range and record thick length, thin length, A width, I width and Z separation at each.
Measure band widths from the boundaries actually placed in the scene rather than from the same expressions that positioned the meshes, so a placement error is visible.
Drive the parameter past full overlap and confirm the stated rejection or clamping rule fires.
observable_checks: Thick and thin filament lengths are identical at all five samples to the precision of the geometry; any change identifies a uniform-scale defect.
A-band width stays constant while Z separation and I-band width decrease; the direction of change is the observable, not a calibrated value.

A parameter beyond full overlap follows the declared rule, whether that is rejection with a message or clamping at the valid end; drawing an unclamped invalid configuration silently is the failure signal.

known_limits: Schematic geometry with a dimensionless shortening parameter; no calibrated ultrastructure, force or fatigue behaviour is implied.
Authored verification guidance; no scene was run or rendered for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: When a sarcomere contracts the Z lines move closer together and the I band becomes smaller, while the A band stays the same width.
claims.scope: Skeletal-muscle sarcomere under the sliding-filament model as described in the cited section; qualitative geometry, not a force model or calibrated dimensions.

source_refs.locator: The Sliding Filament Model of Contraction, Z lines and band widths
